Rep. Ron Estes highlights federal spending oversight and election security concerns
Rep. Ron Estes, U.S. Congressman representing Kansas’ 4th district since 2017, posted a series of statements on social media addressing federal spending oversight, election security, and commemorating the late Sen. Bob Dole.
On July 21, 2026, Estes highlighted recent efforts by the Treasury Department to prevent improper payments: ".@SecScottBessent announced today that the Treasury stopped nearly 100 million of taxpayer dollars from being paid to deceased people, thanks to commonsense legislation that was signed into law by @POTUS in February. I spoke in strong support of the Ending Improper Payments to https://t.co/XA78mkdsbN".
The following day, July 22, he addressed concerns about foreign involvement in state elections: "Foreign money should be kept out of Kansas elections once and for all. Right now, a dangerous back door in the law allows foreign adversaries to launder dark money into our elections through nonprofit activists. Today I spoke in strong support of the Stopping Foreign Influence in https://t.co/2ovakKOkj8".
Later on July 22, Estes marked what would have been the birthday of Sen. Bob Dole: "Sen. Bob Dole was an American hero who hailed from the Sunflower State, and today would have been his 103rd birthday. He was a personal inspiration to me, and I always admired his genuine devotion and service to our country. But even more than that, he was a deeply kind and https://t.co/cNRdlf9gtV".
Estes has represented Kansas’s 4th District since replacing Mike Pompeo in 2017. Born in Topeka in 1956 and currently residing in Wichita, Estes holds a Bachelor of Science degree from Tennessee Technological University.
